proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: Working with the correspondence between irreducible components through a point and minimal primes of the local ring, the base change of lemma-groupoid-on-field-explain-points makes the source and target maps isomorphisms, and faithful flat local maps transfer uniqueness of minimal primes back, while the move-point automorphism reduces part (1) to part (2). In the separably closed case, the product of two irreducible components through the identity is irreducible and its composition image is an irreducible set containing both components: for a T-valued point of either component the identity axiom c(x, e composed with s composed with x) = x together with e lying on the other component exhibits each component inside the image, forcing them equal. In general the separable algebraic closure has a unique component through the lifted identity, faithful flatness reflects this to uniqueness on R, and the Galois orbit lemma with the one-point fibre over the identity gives invariance of the component, i.e. geometric irreducibility via s and via t. core_obligations: Fix the convention that irreducible components through r correspond to minimal primes of the local ring at r (proof lines 1455-1458). Choose the base change k' and point r' of the restriction with s, t isomorphisms by lemma-groupoid-on-field-explain-points; the local ring map is faithfully flat and local (lemma-restrict-groupoid-on-field), so uniqueness of the minimal prime at r' implies it at r; the move-point automorphism (lemma-groupoid-on-field-move-point) carries the identity to r, so part (1) follows from part (2) (proof lines 1455-1469). In the separably closed case take two irreducible components X, Y through e: their fibre product over the source and target maps is irreducible (varieties lemmas 038F and 020J), and its composition image is irreducible in R; for a T-valued point x of X the identity axiom gives c(x, e composed with s composed with x) = x with the second factor factoring through Y since e lies on Y, so X lies in the image, and symmetrically Y, whence the image equals both and X = Y (proof lines 1471-1484). In general pass to the separable algebraic closure k': the restriction has a unique component Z' through e'; since the restriction map to the intermediate base change is faithfully flat and e' maps to e'', there is exactly one component Z'' of the base change through e'', and faithful flatness of the base change to R reflects uniqueness back to exactly one component Z of R through e, proving (2) (proof lines 1486-1500). For (3), any irreducible component Z''' of the base change of Z is a Galois translate of Z'' (varieties-lemma-orbit-irreducible-components, tag 04KY); the Galois action fixes e'' because the fibre over e is the single point e'' so e'' lies in every translate, and uniqueness forces Z''' = Z''; hence the base change of Z is irreducible, which is geometric irreducibility over k via s, and the same argument via t finishes (proof lines 1502-1512).
proof_roadmap: Reduce part (1) to part (2) by the explain-points base change, faithful flat local transfer, and the move-point automorphism (proof lines 1455-1469).
Prove uniqueness of the component through e over a separably closed field by irreducibility of the product and the T-valued point identity-axiom argument (proof lines 1471-1484).
Descend uniqueness to a general field through the separable algebraic closure and faithful flatness (proof lines 1486-1500).
Prove geometric irreducibility via the Galois orbit lemma and the one-point fibre over e, for s and for t (proof lines 1502-1512).
